item.title: AngularJS Clean URLs: Implementing HTML5 History Mode to Remove Hashtags
item.description:
“AngularJS Clean URLs: Implementing HTML5 History Mode to Remove Hashtags”

How does one transition AngularJS routing from the default hashbang (#!) scheme to the cleaner, server-friendly HTML5 History API, and what critical server-side adjustments are necessary to support this configuration?

By default, AngularJS utilizes the hashbang fragment (#) in URLs for client-side routing, which is compatible with older browsers but results in URLs like example.com/#/about. To achieve clean, SEO-optimized URLs such as example.com/about, you must enable HTML5 mode via $locationProvider.html5Mode(true). However, this change requires specific client-side HTML setup and robust server-side URL rewriting to direct all relevant requests back to your main application entry point (index.html).

item.title: Implementing Dynamic CMS Routes in ASP.NET MVC with Custom RouteBase
item.description:
“Implementing Dynamic CMS Routes in ASP.NET MVC with Custom RouteBase”

How does one achieve flexible, content-managed system (CMS)-style routing—where URLs map directly to database content identifiers—within the traditional ASP.NET MVC routing pipeline? The accepted method involves creating a specialized route handler by deriving from RouteBase.

This approach requires implementing two critical overrides: GetRouteData to process incoming HTTP requests into recognizable route values, and GetVirtualPath to construct URLs from route values (reverse routing).

item.title: Angular Router: Effective Strategies for Passing Data Between Components
item.description:
“Angular Router: Effective Strategies for Passing Data Between Components”

Navigating between views in an Angular application frequently requires sending information from a source component to a destination component. Since Angular 2+, several mechanisms have emerged to facilitate this data transfer, each suited for different scenarios regarding visibility in the URL and persistence across page reloads. How does an expert architect choose the right method for inter-component communication during routing?

Utilizing Static Route data Configuration

One fundamental approach involves embedding static data directly into the route configuration itself. This data is available immediately upon route activation.
